summary: Sound, already-proven kernel port that replaces exactly the two incumbent split-KV kernels (A 112.7 + B 8.4 us at decode_16, 248.5 + 8.6 at decode_32 in c243a29f) at an unchanged config gate. Judge it on the replaced-kernel rows: the headline gain (~0.5-1%) is below the CI width. Port the kernel from attention master c3c1b01 (s2 path = template <4,true,false>) rather than the s2 branch, so the sibling full-decode1-two-level-ticket-port becomes a disjoint batch==1 gate on the same module.
justification: A. Mechanism: the hypothesis's replaced work is kernel A (persistent 2 CTA/SM, strided 1024-token chunks) plus kernel B (separate LSE combine + norm-gate). Stream-K over 64-token tiles gives each CTA an equal, contiguous range, which removes the agentic-length tail and the strided page-table walk. The per-request ticket folds B into the last-arriving CTA and drops one graph node. On the same H200 judge, muse_attention_decode measured the same kernel as follows. decode_16: 119.3 us (A+B) -> 108.9 us (s2 e592b1f5) and 110.1 us (s3 2a324178). decode_32: 254.1 -> 226.8 and 225.6. Both runs passed 16/16 tests with no fault on sm_90a. Decode_layer's incumbent rows are nearly identical (A 112.7 vs 111.4; A 248.5 vs 245.5), so the 106-108 and 226-230 us targets transfer directly. The KV floor (~63/126 us) is far above L2, so the surrounding layer's L2 state should not change the kernel's bandwidth. At T=16/32 the dense chain is active and the side stream is unused, so the kernel runs alone on the GPU with the same occupancy assumptions as in attention. Expected shapes and directions are consistent. The gate is unchanged (full, q_len 1, page 1, 1<B<=64, tp8), so decode_1, sliding and verify_* stay flat. Weight 16 per full decode shape means only about -13 us at decode_16 (306.7 -> ~294, ~4%) and about -27 us at decode_32 (479.6 -> ~452, ~6%). That is roughly 0.5-1% on the headline, inside the +/-1.5% CI. Marlin rows on these shapes swing 10-30 us run to run (kv-bw-3p5: Marlin 95.9 -> 106.9 at decode_16, 111.2 -> 144.7 at decode_32), so even the per-shape totals can hide a 9-12 us kernel gain. Read splitkv_attn_sk_kernel's top_kernels row against 121.1/257.1 (kill >= 116/245, as written). WEAKEST LINK: the prepare-time selector. prepare(weights) has no config, so 'timing at the gated batch' must use synthetic B=16/32. With uniform lengths, stream-K's advantage (the ragged tail) is smallest and tickets vs kernel B is a ~8 us difference, so a noisy CUDA-event comparison could silently keep A/B. The run would then read as 'flat' while measuring the incumbent. Use agentic-style ragged synthetic lengths at 80000 ctx, choose per batch (16 and 32 separately) with a small margin, and print PATH CHOSEN per batch so the profile row can be read as which kernel actually ran. A secondary weak point: prepare cannot size the workspace 'from config', so use a fixed MAXB=64 x (grid + B) allocation (~1.3 MB, as in the s3 code's slots <= grid + B).
confounders: full-decode-splitkv-restack-on-pdl: the incumbent being replaced, not a confounder. The port must keep its q prep (q.view(tokens,16,64).to(FP8).contiguous()), read gate through qkv.stride(0) like splitkv_combine, and keep v_scale and RMS_EPS exactly as kernel B does. A mismatch there shows up as a test failure, not a timing confound.

small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl: active at T=16/32 (DL_MAX_TOKENS=32) but downstream of the o GEMM. The attention kernels are plain <<<>>> launches with no PDL edge, so the only interaction is the one fewer graph node (~1-3 us), which counts as part of this change. It also keeps the side stream off at these shapes, so no concurrent kernels skew stream-K's static partition.
fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched: inactive on the gated shapes (paired requires 'not splitkv'), so no confound.
stack-align-par-sidestream-sliding1: its side-stream dispatch runs only at T>32 (verify_16/32), outside the gate, so no concurrency with the attention kernel.

Sibling full-decode1-two-level-ticket-port (queued alongside, not landed): same kernel family, disjoint gate (batch == 1 vs 1 < batch <= 64), so each run attributes cleanly. Attention master c3c1b01 holds both paths in one template: TWO=false is this port's B>1 single-level ticket at grid 2xSM; TWO=true is the sibling's B=1 two-level ticket at grid = SM count. In attention, adding TWO left B>1 flat (108.9/226.8 -> 110.1/225.6 us). Both ports built separately from master will conflict when restacked (same module and gate code), and the second lander must restack. If both take the kernel source from c3c1b01 under one module name, the second becomes a gate/grid edit only. The sibling's text 'batch>1 keeps master kernel A/B' goes stale if this one lands first.
interference: No companion is warranted. Kind is rewrite stage 3, judged on the replaced kernels' own rows (splitkv_attn_sk_kernel vs splitkv_attn_kernel + splitkv_combine_kernel), and those rows separate cleanly. The gate is config-only and unchanged, and nothing landed overlaps the gated shapes (pairing is off, PDL is not on the attention edge, the side stream is idle at T<=32). An ab-revert of the incumbent restack would just compare against paired FA3, which is already known. A control isolating stream-K from ticket-fold would only re-measure attention's s2 diagnostics (stream-K with and without ticket), so ask for those in-process prints instead of a separate check. The one ambiguity is which path the prepare selector actually picked. That is a logging requirement (per-batch PATH CHOSEN plus selector timings), not a companion run.
rules_flags: Ticket / gticket buffers are zero-initialised scratch, not derived from inputs: OK. Allocate them outside graph capture (import or first prepare), and zero them again after the in-process self-check and diagnostics (attention s3 re-zeroes in prepare), so a check that faults or aborts cannot leave stale counts for the timed graph.

The last arrival must LSE-merge the slots in fixed slot order (c_lo..c_hi), not arrival order, so results stay deterministic. The fp32 merge is required. No precision issue: f16 MMA on e4m3-widened values is exact, the same as the incumbent.

Every key is attended: stream-K covers every tile of every request's cache_seqlens[b] (including the token just stored by store_cache). The self-check should include a request whose seq % 64 is in 1..7 and one shorter than 64 (attention s2 did; the hypothesis's B list {2,5,16,32,33} should cover these explicitly).

The prepare-time CUDA-event selector and diagnostics stay in prepare; kernel_fn has no sync, timing or host read. Master already calls torch.empty for the workspace inside kernel_fn, and the hypothesis moves it to prepare. That is fine, but confirm one shared workspace is never used by two layers at once (it is not: single main stream at T<=32).
No child process: the in-process canary/self-check required by LESSONS is specified. Keep the build to sm_90a only, as written.
open_questions: Will the implementer port from attention master c3c1b01 (s2 kernel plus the unused TWO template path) or from the s2 branch f291b49? c3c1b01 is preferred so the batch-1 sibling reuses the same module.
Selector inputs: which synthetic length distribution and batch values? Uniform 80000 understates stream-K's benefit. Does it choose per batch (16 vs 32) or once for all gated batches?

Workspace sizing without config in prepare: fixed MAXB=64 x (2*SMs + 64) slots, or allocated per call as attention s2 did? The hypothesis says 'no allocation in kernel_fn', but master already allocates there.

The decode_layer profile is dist=soft while attention is dist=coherent. That is the MoE routing distribution and does not affect attention, but confirm the agentic KV-length spread is the same generator in both problems.
